verbs.definition: find a solution to a problem
verbs.example: It's taken me all evening to figure out how to turn on this new television.

verbs.definition: find out if someone or something is acceptable
verbs.example: Femmy's thinking of moving to a new part of town, so she went to check out the area.

verbs.definition: ask a skilled person to deal with a problem for you
verbs.example: One of the pipes was leaking, so we called in a plumber to fix it.

verbs.definition: go to someone for help or advice
verbs.example: Whenever Gitanjali has a problem, she turns to her grandmother for advice.
Jessica has been keeping the name of her new boyfriend from me.
Paolo has prepared a new sculpture for the exhibition. I've asked him what it is, but he's not giving anything away!

verbs.definition: begin to understand or realize something
verbs.example: I only cottoned onto the fact that Lisa and Pete were dating when I saw them at the ice rink together.

verbs.definition: enter a room or building suddenly
verbs.example: We were all eating our dinner when the dog burst into the room.
I was bowled over when Nadia announced that she had been accepted into dance school.
Kamal was blown away by Jose's account of his adventures in the Amazon.

verbs.definition: approach someone quietly to surprise them
verbs.example: Mollie crept up on her grandfather while he slept in the garden.
My best friend sprang it on me last night that she's moving to Canada.

verbs.definition: understand or accept some news or information
verbs.example: The surprising news was a lot to take in.

verbs.definition: say something suddenly, without thinking about it
verbs.example: My little sister blurted out to Dad that we'd organized a surprise party for him. She can't keep a secret.
I didn't mean to tell the team that it was your birthday. It just slipped out.
Clara can't believe she passed her medical exams. It's going to take a while for it to sink in.
The movie star tried to hush up the fact that she had a new boyfriend.

verbs.definition: pretend something is true or that you believe in something
verbs.example: My daughter often pretends to be a dinosaur. We all have to play along with her.
People have woken up to the fact that we need to look after the environment.
While I was on vacation in Venice, I bumped into one of my cousins. I couldn't believe it.
I was shopping at the antiques market when I stumbled upon a valuable necklace.
I was taken aback when Tia and Juan told me they were getting married.
Hetty's career as a musician came about after a producer saw her performing.
When I tried to log into my account, a message came up saying that my account had been blocked.

verbs.definition: appear, become available, start to exist
verbs.example: Staying in touch with friends became much easier once the internet came along.

verbs.definition: leave a room, building, or enclosed space
verbs.example: Ben and Eleanor came out of the toy store with presents for their grandchildren.

verbs.definition: move across a room, space, country, etc.
verbs.example: Natsuo came across the room to speak to us.

verbs.definition: experience something negative (such as criticism, threat, or attack)
verbs.example: The company has come under attack for its high carbon emissions.
Derek sat down in front of the TV when the ten o'clock news came on.
My daughter's still waiting for her results to come through. She's so nervous.
No matter how much we clean it, this graffiti won't come off the wall.
Lots of talented people make up our circus's team of acrobats.

verbs.definition: manage to see, hear, or understand
verbs.example: Luanne struggled to make out what the train conductor was saying.
With hot weather expected, thousands of tourists made for the coast.
We were about to eat dinner when the dog made off with the leg of lamb.
When I asked Kim what she made of Toshi's new novel, she said she loved it.
Emily is doing up her house at the moment. It's going to look great when she's finished.

verbs.definition: abolish, no longer need or use
verbs.example: With so many people using bank cards, we may be able to do away with cash in the future.

verbs.definition: do something to solve a problem
verbs.example: The council needs to decide what it's going to do about the city's litter problem.
Riya was very disappointed with her wedding cake, and insisted it be done over.

verbs.definition: complete a task you don't want to do
verbs.example: Let's just clean the kitchen now and get it over with.
Claude got up from his chair and went to make some more tea.

verbs.definition: start to focus on a task
verbs.example: It's almost eleven o'clock. We should get down to work.
Can you help me get the shopping in, please?

verbs.definition: avoid an obstacle, deal with a problem
verbs.example: Chad's oven had broken, but he got around it by using the microwave instead.

verbs.definition: find a way over an obstacle
verbs.example: Cheryl's dog keeps getting over the fence into the neighbor's backyard.

verbs.definition: remove something (from a bag, box, room, etc.)
verbs.example: Lee got his fishing rod out of the garage and carried it to his car.
Ramona always gets her message across, even when she's explaining complicated scientific theories.

verbs.definition: retrieve something from a higher position
verbs.example: Glen climbed the ladder to get the cat down from the tree.
Before accusing Simon, the police had to get their facts together.
As soon as we got to the ski resort, we went straight to the slopes.
After Gia was rude to me, I got back at her by not inviting her to my wedding.

verbs.definition: begin (about something unpleasant that may last a long time)
verbs.example: As Martin walked home late at night, fear began to set in.

verbs.definition: activate, cause something to start happening
verbs.example: Harry burned the dinner and set off the smoke detector.
The bad weather has set us back by two weeks. We won't finish building the bridge until November.

verbs.definition: make someone or something special in comparison to others
verbs.example: Lee's speed sets him apart from the other players in the tournament.
After leaving school, Romesh set up his own business selling surfboards.

verbs.definition: order someone or something to attack someone
verbs.example: The security guard threatened to set his dog on us if we didn't leave immediately.
Mary set out all her qualifications and experience in her resume.

verbs.definition: start tackling a problem or task
verbs.example: How are you going to go about fixing this car?
As soon as I realized Orla had forgotten her bag, I went after her.
James went over the company's accounts to check for mistakes.
After I got back from the dentist, it took a couple of hours for the pain to go away.

verbs.definition: be the opposite of what you wish or believe
verbs.example: Buying water in plastic bottles goes against my principles.

verbs.definition: enter a building, room, or enclosed space
verbs.example: A team of firefighters went into the burning building.

verbs.definition: leave a room, building, or enclosed space
verbs.example: As soon as the teacher had gone out of the room, the children began misbehaving.
Help yourself to some cakes. There are enough to go around.
Malachai went through a period of unhappiness after his dog died.
There's something going on next door. I can hear loud music.
Parents often have to go without sleep when they have a new baby.
Cath couldn't find the recipe, so she had to make it up as she went along.
Kelly's decided to go for the job at the software company. It's very well paid.
All the money we make today will go toward funding the new school library.

verbs.definition: move from a higher position to a lower one
verbs.example: Rob and I sat on the beach watching the sun go down.

verbs.definition: decide to do something (after consideration or official approval)
verbs.example: Even though it was a cloudy day, Ramon decided to go ahead with the picnic.

verbs.definition: know someone for a long time
verbs.example: Michelle and I go back years. I've known her since kindergarten.

verbs.definition: be called by a certain name
verbs.example: My new trainer is called Zachariah, though he usually goes by Zac.

verbs.definition: move from a lower position to a higher one
verbs.example: The children watched the hot-air balloon slowly go up into the air.

verbs.definition: place something you have been carrying on the ground or a surface
verbs.example: The deliveryman put the parcel down before knocking on the door.
Liam finished decorating the cake and put it on a stand.
Angela is upset about her divorce, but she's trying to put it behind her.
Can you please be quiet? You're putting me off!
The fitness instructor put the class through a tough training program.
Forecasters have put out a weather warning for heavy rain and strong winds.
Cassie followed the instructions carefully to put her new wardrobe together.
Scarlett had to put up with busy trains every day on her way to work.
Nousha's room looked much nicer after she'd put up some pictures.

verbs.definition: return an object to its proper place
verbs.example: After finishing the gardening, Scott put his tools away.

verbs.definition: return an object to its original place
verbs.example: After painting the living room, Paul and Sally put all the furniture back.

verbs.definition: take someone to a quieter place to tell them something in private
verbs.example: Amara took her mother aside to tell her that she was pregnant.

verbs.definition: take someone or something with you
verbs.example: Jim's mother asked him to take his younger brother along to the skate park.
The waste collectors came to take away the bags of trash.

verbs.definition: get something from a higher place
verbs.example: Denise took a jar down from the shelf to give her dog a biscuit.
Seeing the black clouds, Tim went outside to take the washing in.
The police stopped the criminal and took the stolen money off him.
Eliza has really taken to golf. She never thought she'd like it.

verbs.definition: take someone or something to a higher level
verbs.example: The elevator took James up to the top floor of the building.
Martha played the violin as a child, but gave it up when she left school.

verbs.definition: give something to people for free
verbs.example: The cafe on the high street is giving out free samples of their new cakes.

verbs.definition: agree to do something after some resistance
verbs.example: My son had been asking for an ice cream all day. I finally gave in and bought him one.

verbs.definition: give something to someone for free (rather than selling it)
verbs.example: Tom's moving to a smaller apartment so he's giving away some of his belongings.

verbs.definition: tell someone or something to leave you alone
verbs.example: Go away!

verbs.definition: tell someone or something to follow you or to move faster
verbs.example: Come on!

verbs.definition: tell someone to leave a room in an angry way
verbs.example: Get out!

verbs.definition: warn someone about something they haven't noticed yet
verbs.example: Look out!

verbs.definition: said when you're confident and ready to start doing something
verbs.example: Are you ready to start? Yes, bring it on!

verbs.definition: let someone know it is fine for them to start talking
verbs.example: Hey Vi, can I ask you something? Sure, fire away.

verbs.definition: said to express disbelief at something someone has said
verbs.example: Come off it!

verbs.definition: said when inviting someone into a room or building (especially your own home)
verbs.example: Hi Carolina! Come in.

verbs.definition: said when giving someone permission to do something
verbs.example: Do you mind if I sit here? Go ahead.
